actual.value:
This project aimed to train 20 lecturers professors and university staff on 2 main topics: horticulture (especially green house farming practises and Climate Smart Farming) and entrepreneurship. Both topics have been addressed as per plan and project design. The project also included a production pilot for both open field and greenhouses, fieldtrip and excursions. The Digital training game : farming Forward (Kucheza) was introduced to all participants as part of the entrepreneurship development programme. In total 21 participants fully completed the training programme (one drop oyut due to maternity leave). Horticultural training: a total of 8 training were organised of which 7 online and 1 physical training. All training topics were addressed and several topics were refreshed in the physical training. Entrepreneurial trainings: as per plan, out of 4 training 3 were conducted online and 1 was conducted physical (the last one). The physical one included a pitching event of 4 groups, presenting their final business case towards potential investors. This was a major highlight of the whole TMT, as we invited various potential (real) investors the 4 trainings were provided
ToT game based learning: Kucheza conducted throughout the project period online game based learning session, often in close coordination with the entrepreneurial training, as topics were much overlapping. In addition Kucheza, facilitated extra game based learning sessions for a few highly interested participants that are seriously considering and preparing to use the game with students, also after the project ends.
All the training materials as used during this TMT have been shared with all participants using a google drive, accessible for all of them. The materials can be used by the participants for design new short term courses and/or curricula for students.
Outputs realised: 1. 21 participants trained on Climate Smart Agriculture (open field/ protected cultivation). During the horticultural training focus was more on protected cultivation, as this is where most of the knowledge and skills gaps are currently. The BUK-CDA has several greenhouses, but there is very little knowledge and experience with protected horticulture 9as compared to open field). Hence emphasis was on protected horticulture, including all elements of greenhouse framing. For open field, drop irrigation was applied, for tomatoes and water melon. That is an example of CSF. Focus was also on IPM, well balanced used or fertilisers etc. The training were always including practical’s and skill development> With the active participation of Nigerian based Leventis, it was possible to go with a physical present trainer to the greenhouses or open field to develop skills, showcase practical’s etc. this way of blended learning was quite successful. 2. Blended learning methods and tools have been practised and shared extensively during this TMT+ and the various participants can apply lessons learn in their own future development and application of courses and curricula. 3. AE05 The trained lectures, professors and farm staff are more capable of guiding students on greenhouse farming and Climate Smart farming, being new topics to them. With the training materials that were freely shared, BUK-CDA can further adapt or develop trainings courses and curricula now. BUK_CDA has made an overview of possible new courses but development of the same will require more time. Due to lock down and the ongoing industrial strikes, there is delay. And developing new courses also takes time. But the concepts and ingredients are now with BUK-CDA 4. AE03: ToT in horticulture and entrepreneurship organised based on game based learning made available to 22 participants. All had access to a tablet and the game. The use of the game was truly integrated into various modules. 5. AE03 :Game Based learning> a group of around 8 participants took key interest and active participation in the game based learning session. The BUK-CDA has one training room equipped with about 25 high quality computers (for GIS) and this can be used as the training venue for the farming forward game with students. It should be notes that students usually do not have their own tablet, and can also not afford to buy one, so alternatives need to be founds, such as using this computer raining room. Kucheza has invested some extra time in this selected group of teachers for some additional coaching
Most important milestones: 1. Lot of inside skills and knowledge created about protected agriculture, and how to transfer this knowledge also to the next generation of students(this is completely lacking in curricula of universities and TVETs) 2. Entrepreneurship development in a very pragmatic approach : working from the beginning in a group on a business idea, that became more and more developed and resulted in an almost real life pitching event! 3. Introduction of the farming forward game and adoption by some teachers already to practice this also with students 4. Field visits to various corners of Nigeria to observe and learn from other projects and companies and NGOs in the country.

comment.narrative:
03-06-2022: The majority of the BUK-CDA teachers and staff have their own farms on the outskirts of Kano, living in the rural areas. Several of them have reported that they have applied new skills and practises on their own farms, and they invite other farmers to observe what they are doing. One of the expected outcomes of the project also referred to supporting 22 farmer communities that are supported by BUK-CDA. Due to COVID19, it was very complex to organise any trainings or meetings, but informal exposure and exchange definitely took place.
Direct beneficiaries of this program are the 22 trained lectures and staff of BUK-CDA Indirect participants are: 1. Students that are already introduced to game based learning (done by 2 -3 teachers) 2. Workers on the BUK-CDA farm: they were invited to join the practical sessions in the greenhouse or on the farm and in this way they also benefited from the programme 3. Neighbours of the active lectures that have put into practise what they have learned on their own farms
